| [NOTE-422](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-422.md) | Comments on a derivation and application of the ‘maximum entropy production’ principle | Two corrections to Dewar. | [NOTE-456](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-456.md) | Participatory sense-making: An enactive approach to social cognition | An enactive account of social cognition built on coordination dynamics. When coordination and the encounter shape each other, the interaction gains its own precarious operational closure; it is social only if the interactors stay autonomous. Coordinated sense-making then ranges from one partner's sense-making being modulated to meanings made jointly. Conceptual throughout; evidence is illustrative (corridor, charades, mother–infant timing, perceptual crossing). | Read |
| [NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md) | Defining Agency: Individuality, Normativity, Asymmetry, and Spatio-temporality in Action | Minimal agency needs a self-individuated system that is the source of modulations of its coupling with the environment and regulates them by norms it generates. An autonomous organization, a precarious network of mutually enabling processes, generates all three when it adaptively modulates its coupling for its own maintenance. Life is sufficient, not necessary. The definition is a proposal: the authors say asymmetry's formalization is incomplete and modeller-relative. | Read |
| [NOTE-467](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-467.md) | The Haken–Kelso–Bunz (HKB) model: from matter to movement to mind | Kelso's retrospective on HKB. The relative-phase equation dφ/dt = −a sin φ − 2b sin 2φ has stable in-phase and anti-phase states for b/a > 1/4 and only in-phase below; with noise the switch is a nonequilibrium phase transition with critical fluctuations and slowing. Symmetry breaking gives metastability (relative coordination); merged with Kuramoto it models groups. The same dynamics is reported within and between people and in brain activity. A first-person account, not a review. | Read |
| [NOTE-468](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-468.md) | Biological organisation as closure of constraints | A constraint acts on a process while being conserved at that process's time scale; closure is a set of constraints, each directly dependent on and generative for another, that cannot be split. This separates closure from cycles of processes, grounds functions, and gives a boundary criterion, refined by a preliminary count-based tendency to closure for symbionts and by nested separated closures for levels. Applied only to schematic examples; closure is not claimed to define organisms. | Read |
| [NOTE-502](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-502.md) | Interacting spiral wave patterns underlie complex brain dynamics | Phase fields of 0.01–0.1 Hz HCP fMRI on the flattened cortex hold about 16 spirals per hemisphere at rest (radius 10.5 ± 4.8 mm), centred on phase singularities that move at 2.2 mm/s with superdiffusive exponent β ≈ 1.5 and sit on functional boundaries. Opposite spirals annihilate (51% fully, 46% partly), like ones repel (2.6%). Spiral centres and charges decode four language conditions at 48.3% (chance 25%, raw-amplitude decoder 30.2%), and spiral pairs act as gates and walls that route task activity flow. | Read |
| [NOTE-509](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-509.md) | Ultraviolet Superradiance from Mega-Networks of Tryptophan in Biological Architectures | A radiative non-Hermitian Hamiltonian for N tryptophan 1La dipoles (single excitation) predicts superradiant states in microtubule architectures (max Γ/γ ≈ 4000 in a centriole, ≈ 7000 extrapolated for bundles) and a thermal quantum yield that grows with size and is insensitive to static disorder up to 200 cm⁻¹. Steady-state spectroscopy gives tryptophan QY 17.6 ± 2.1% in microtubules against 10.6 ± 0.6% in tubulin dimers. No lifetimes were measured, so the radiative rate is inferred, not observed. | Read |
| [NOTE-555](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-555.md) | Conceptualization of the Holobiont Paradigm as It Pertains to Corals | A mini-review arguing that corals must be studied as holobionts. The holobiont is defined by location (coral plus microbiota in body, mucus and skeleton), and its membership can change. Traits belong to host–symbiont combinations: a novel anemone–alga pairing out-performed both natural ones in oxygen flux at 32–34 °C, and two octocorals lost symbionts by different routes, one per host cell and one with host cells. It asks, without answering, whether the holobiont is the unit of selection. | Read |
| [NOTE-556](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-556.md) | Defining Coral Bleaching as a Microbial Dysbiosis within the Coral Holobiont | A review that redefines bleaching as three holobiont dysbiosis stages: microbial buffering, Symbiodiniaceae reorganisation by shuffling or switching, and traumatic dysbiosis ending in death (Figure 3). The supporting material is cited and correlational. Vibrio rose from about 0 to 30% relative abundance in bleached corals and returned in resilient ones, but the authors say cause and consequence cannot be separated. "Dysbiosis" names both the disruption and the healthy adaptive response, and the stages have no operational boundaries. | Read |
| [NOTE-557](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-557.md) | Signaling cascades and the importance of moonlight in coral broadcast mass spawning | Two experiments at Heron Island on Acropora millepora. In 2011, colonies under ambient night light (N = 6) spawned with the reef, while colonies lit after sunset (N = 5) or kept dark (N = 5) did not spawn that night. 184 transcripts selected by variance changed around gamete release only in ambient colonies. In 2006, 90 colonies under blue, green or white nocturnal light spawned 6–8 h or two nights late, and under red light on time. The GPCR and melanopsin cascade is a model built from correlated expression. | Read |
| [NOTE-558](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-558.md) | Phase Shifts, Herbivory, and the Resilience of Coral Reefs to Climate Change | Four roofless 25 m² cages on Orpheus Island's reef crest kept large and medium fishes out for 30 months after the 1998 bleaching, against four partial cages and four open plots. Macroalgae averaged 56% cover in cages and 4.1% and 1.7% outside. Coral cover reached 7.7% inside against 19.2% and 20.2%. Recruitment fell to about a third (39 against 108 and 118 per 25 m²) and mortality of established colonies was 24.2% against 9.8% and 11.3%. Reopened, the cages lost their algae in 30 days. | Read |
| [NOTE-571](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-571.md) | Catastrophic regime shifts in ecosystems: linking theory to observation | A review of how to tell whether an ecosystem has alternative stable states. Field patterns (jumps, multimodality, dual relationships) are suggestive and never conclusive, since a stepwise driver or a simple threshold produces them too. Experiments can come close to proof: initial-state dependence, lasting shifts after temporary disturbance, and hysteresis. Models show positive feedback must be strong enough. | Read |
| [NOTE-572](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-572.md) | Resilience and Stability of Ecological Systems | Ecological theory had equated stability with behaviour near equilibrium. Holling separates stability (return to equilibrium) from resilience (the capacity to absorb change and persist, set by the domain of attraction), shows they can trade off in lakes, forests, insects and fish, and warns that managing for constant yield can erode resilience. | Read |
| [NOTE-576](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-576.md) | The Method of Characteristics Revisited: A Viability Approach | Viability is a property of a constraint set under a dynamics: K is viable if from every state some evolution stays in K, invariant if all do. Nagumo's theorem reduces viability to a tangency condition. When K is not viable, the viability kernel is the largest viable part of it, and everything else in K leaves in finite time. Stability in the Lyapunov sense is not discussed. | Read |
| [NOTE-577](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-577.md) | The Viable System Model: Its Provenance, Development, Methodology and Pathology | Beer's retrospective on the Viable System Model. Five subsystems are necessary and sufficient for any organism or organization to keep its identity independently, and the structure recurs at every level. The model is defended as a scientific model built by homomorphic mapping, testable but never proved. Pathologies are traced to failing subsystems, chiefly the collapse of Three and Five when Four is missing. Evidence is the author's recollected consultancy. | Read |
| [NOTE-584](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-584.md) | Risk management in a dynamic society: a modelling problem | Risk management is a control problem across a sociotechnical hierarchy. Under cost and effort gradients, activity migrates toward the boundary of acceptable performance, and redundant defences erode unobserved because breaching one shows no effect. Accidents come from the interaction of many locally reasonable decisions. The remedy is making boundaries visible, not suppressing errors. | Read |
| [NOTE-655](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-655.md) | Irreversibility in bacterial regulatory networks | In an ensemble of sign-consistent Boolean rules on the 87-gene core of the E. coli regulatory network, 51 genes admit a transient knockout or overexpression that leaves the network in a different attractor; only genes that reach a positive circuit can, and the likelihood grows with the weighted number of paths to one. Transitions run from small basins to large. The comparison with evolved crp-knockout strains supports the network's sign structure strongly and its irreversibility predictions only weakly; no transient perturbation was done in cells. | Read |
| [NOTE-656](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-656.md) | A. baumannii PmrB oxidative-stress response memory | An unrefereed bioRxiv preprint arguing that the PmrA/PmrB two-component system in Acinetobacter baumannii senses sublethal oxidative stress through a periplasmic histidine box coordinating a nickel cofactor, activates iron-sulfur repair and peroxide-scavenging genes, holds a redox-gated conformational switch (from simulation), and retains a 30--90 min "response memory" that primes cross-protection against lethal peroxide and antimicrobial peptides and is required for virulence in mice and hypervirulence in a clinical isolate. | Read |
| [NOTE-657](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-657.md) | Bhattacharyya et al. 2023, heritable iron memory in E. coli | In genetically identical E. coli, a single cell's swarming potential is shared by its descendants for about four generations and lost by seven; it tracks the cell's iron status as read by a Fur-repressed reporter (low iron, better swarmer), iron manipulation lengthens it, and a three-class switching model fits the lineages only if each founding cell holds its class for a fixed delay before switching. The iron link is a correlation through a promoter reporter, and the model is fitted to two time points. | Read |
| [NOTE-670](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-670.md) | An argument for hyperbolic geometry in neural circuits | A perspective, not a result: hyperbolic geometry should suit neural circuits because it approximates trees, makes networks navigable, and shares with Zipf's law an exponential growth of states. The Zipf link is an analogy that any power-law rank distribution, and any system with extensive entropy, would satisfy; the case for three dimensions leans on Mostow rigidity, which does not bear on noisy embeddings; and the only data shown are the olfactory embedding of Zhou, Smith & Sharpee (2018). | Read |
| [NOTE-673](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-673.md) | Multiscale unfolding of real networks by geometric renormalization | Defines a renormalization group for networks embedded in the S¹ hidden metric space: merge blocks of angular neighbours, link supernodes if any members were linked. To first order the S¹ model maps into itself (κ′ = (Σκ^β)^{1/β}, β fixed, μ and R over r), so layers are the same ensemble with ⟨k⟩ scaled by r^ν, ν = 2/(γ−1) − 1 or 2/β − 1. Six real networks collapse across layers by eye and keep their communities; downscaled replicas reproduce three dynamics, and multiscale greedy routing succeeds more often. | Read |
| [NOTE-678](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-678.md) | Emergent Hyperbolic Network Geometry | Shows that simplicial complexes grown by gluing d-simplices to (d − 1)-faces, by a rule with no geometry in it, have exponential or power-law degrees (γ = 2 + 1/(d + s − 1)) by a master equation, high clustering and modularity, and a tree as their dual; and draws them, with all links of equal length, as ideal simplices tiling the Poincaré ball. The hyperbolicity is that drawing, which the authors say depends on the equal-length assumption; it is not measured or proved. A fitness on faces gives a simulated transition to growth in one direction. | Read |
| [NOTE-680](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-680.md) | Hyperbolic Geometry of Complex Networks | Shows, for a model in which nodes sit in a hyperbolic disk and connect with a Fermi–Dirac probability of their hyperbolic distance, that the degree distribution is a power law with γ = 2α/ζ + 1 and that clustering is set by a temperature, strongest at T = 0 and gone above T = 1; that a circle-similarity model with power-law hidden degrees is the same ensemble once degree is read as radial depth; and that the configuration model and Erdős–Rényi graphs are its limits with the angular, metric part of the distance removed. Greedy routing by the coordinates is near-optimal and robust in its networks. No real network is embedded. | Read |
| [NOTE-704](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-704.md) | Simon — The Architecture of Complexity | Complexity usually takes the form of hierarchy, defined by intensity of interaction rather than subordination. Hierarchies evolve fast because stable intermediate forms survive interruption, and they are nearly decomposable: fast, nearly independent dynamics inside subsystems; slow, aggregate dynamics between them. The theorem is cited, not shown; the evolutionary numbers are illustrative; the social claims are asserted. | Read |
| [NOTE-724](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-724.md) | Wu & Silva — How Millions Coordinate at Scale | A descriptive study of all three r/place editions plus a coalition-recovery method run on 2017. Participation stays heavy-tailed under the uniform five-minute cap; larger coalitions waste more actions and have lower median activity per member; participants concentrate into large coalitions as an event goes on; and which coalitions survive is barely predictable from their size, area, start time and colour entropy until late. Lasting artworks are those whose coalitions keep working under continual overwriting. | Read |
| [NOTE-725](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-725.md) | Adams, Fernandez & Witkowski — Two Ways of Understanding Social Dynamics | A short, preliminary study of the 2017 canvas alone. Transitions between 10-minute snapshots are tallied as cellular-automaton-style neighbourhood rules, and a CNN predicts each pixel from its 3×3 neighbourhood. Prediction worsens with the horizon and dips in the middle of the event. Locally growing objects are predicted, and designs coordinated off the canvas are missed. There are no baselines or error bars, and participants are never modelled. | Read |
| [NOTE-726](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-726.md) | Hoel, Albantakis & Tononi — Quantifying causal emergence shows that macro can beat micro | Effective information (EI), the mutual information between uniformly imposed interventions on a system's states and their effects, can be higher for a coarse-grained macro description than for the micro description it supervenes on. This happens when coarse-graining makes the mechanisms more deterministic or less degenerate by more than the smaller state space costs. Four toy systems of binary logic gates give gains of 0.40 to 2.92 bits. Causal emergence is defined as that gain. The examples are computed exactly; the reading of the EI peak as the level where causation happens rests on the choice of a uniform intervention distribution at each level, which the paper adopts and does not test. | Read |
| [NOTE-731](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-731.md) | Falmagne, Stephenson & Levin — Interpretable early warnings using machine learning in an online game-experiment | On the 2022 r/place canvas, gradient-boosted trees fed 19 composition-level time series with a 7-hour memory predict the time until a crowd-built image is abruptly overrun, far better than variance or autocorrelation trends, and still work on 2023. The precursors it relies on are many and do not reduce to critical slowing down; a large share of transitions give no warning. The interpretation of the precursors is the authors' conjecture from SHAP curves. | Read |
| [NOTE-733](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-733.md) | Litherland & Mørch — Instruction vs. emergence on r/place | A mixed-methods case study of one 2017 r/place artwork, the Mona Lisa, and its forum, r/monalisaclan. The design was set and revised in the forum through linked blueprints, negotiated with neighbouring communities, and carried out by tens of thousands of placers. A few central forum members could allow or stop proposals. The authors frame the outcome as two control mechanisms, top-down platform rules ("instruction") and bottom-up emergence, and stress that quantitative traces cannot tell cooperation from conflict or reveal affiliation. | Read |
| [NOTE-747](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-747.md) | Watson — Agency, Goal-Directed Behavior, and Part-Whole Relationships | A comparative, scale-relative notion of agency. Given a decomposition into parts with goals of their own, a whole is more agential than its parts when its organization lets them resolve more of their mutual constraints than they would at the equilibrium of the old organization. It shows this as delayed gratification. The essay argues this, and shows in cited models that unsupervised, bottom-up learning can produce such organization. It gives no threshold for an additional agent and no formula beyond comparing total frustration. | Read |
| [NOTE-756](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-756.md) | Varley — Flickering Emergences | Information-theoretic emergence measures built on past–future mutual information are expected values, and their local (pointwise) values can be negative. In a four-node Boolean toy, a coarse-graining that is emergent on average maps about 53% of informative micro transitions to misinformative macro ones, and the whole-to-whole synergy atom is negative for 31.25% of macro transitions. In a connectome, misinformative edges fall mostly between communities. The paper argues the possibility is general to any excess-entropy measure; it shows instances, not a theorem. | Read |
| [NOTE-767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-767.md) | Tononi, Sporns & Edelman — A measure for brain complexity | Defines neural complexity C_N as the summed shortfall of average subset integration below a linear increase with subset size, equivalently the average mutual information across bipartitions summed over sizes. It is zero for independent parts, low for uniformly dependent ones and high when the two coexist. In simulated cortex, patchy grouped connectivity gives higher C_N than the same connections spread randomly. One number for a whole system, with no partition, threshold or penalty. | Read |
| [NOTE-768](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-768.md) | Nowak et al. — Functional Synchronization | A programmatic proposal, offered by its authors "as a heuristic for research agendas": functions at every level from neurons to groups are performed by functional units, which form when lower-level elements synchronize and dissolve when the task ends. Synchronization here means any binding of dynamics, including complementary roles, not convergence on one state. Group synchronization may come from mutual influence or from a common external signal, and the paper treats both alike. | Read |
| [NOTE-773](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-773.md) | Tissot et al. — An ability to respond begins with inner alignment | In a simulated modular coordination game (30 modules of 10 bistable units, strong couplings inside modules, weak across), units that adjust only the phase of their decision cycle toward partners they currently agree with come to synchronise within modules. Each module then switches its convention as one unit in response to the others, and all 50 runs with the learned phases reach a global optimum, against none without. Global synchrony does not do this. Synchrony works by silencing the module's internal pull at a shared moment, not by any signal passed inside it. | Read |
| [NOTE-775](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-775.md) | Pecora et al. — Cluster synchronization and isolated desynchronization | For identical units with identical, symmetric couplings, the orbits of the coupling graph's automorphism group are clusters that can each be exactly synchronized. An irreducible-representation change of coordinates block-diagonalizes the variational equations, so each cluster's stability is computed separately. When the group splits as a direct product, a cluster moved by one factor can lose synchrony while the others keep it. An 11-node electro-optic network showed this as predicted. | Read |
| [NOTE-791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-791.md) v2 | Barnett and Seth — Dynamical independence | A coarse-graining Y = f(X) is dynamically independent when the microscopic history adds nothing to predicting Y beyond Y's own history, given the environment: transfer entropy T(X → Y \| E) = 0. The condition is transformation-invariant and transitive. For linear state-space models it has a closed form, and it is minimized numerically over the Grassmannian. Generically no coarse-graining is exactly independent for VAR order above 1. The minima are many, and the authors treat them all as the "emergence portrait". | Read |
| [NOTE-799](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-799.md) v2 | Luppi et al. — A synergistic workspace for human consciousness | In resting-state fMRI, regions where synergistic interactions outrank redundant ones form a "synergistic workspace". Within it, regions whose synergistic connections spread across more resting-state networks than their redundant ones are classed as gateways (mainly default mode), and the rest as broadcasters (mainly fronto-parietal, lateral prefrontal above all). Pairwise integrated information ΦR falls between DMN gateway regions under propofol (n = 15 or 16; the paper gives both) and in 22 patients with disorders of consciousness against controls, and recovers after anaesthesia, while the original whole-minus-sum Φ shows no common decrease. The increases, near the broadcasters, are not robust. | Read |
| [NOTE-819](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-819.md) | Hopfield — Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities | With symmetric couplings, asynchronous threshold updates descend an energy function, so Hebbian outer-product storage makes random patterns attractors: a cue a few bits off settles into the nearest one. In simulations at N = 30 and 100, recall degrades severely near 0.15N patterns, memories closer than about a tenth of N fuse, and overload makes every memory irretrievable unless old ones are forgotten. | Read |
| [NOTE-831](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-831.md) | Farrell & Ioannou — Generalized Stability Theory I | For a linear system du/dt = Au with A non-normal, the eigenvalues fix only the t → ∞ behaviour. Growth over a finite time t is the largest singular value of e^{At}, bounded below by the fastest mode and at t → 0 set by the numerical abscissa, the top eigenvalue of (A + A†)/2. A system with every mode damped can amplify a perturbation a hundredfold, and its forced and stochastic responses exceed those of the normal system with the same spectrum. | Read |
| [NOTE-839](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-839.md) | Trefethen et al. — Hydrodynamic Stability Without Eigenvalues | The linearized operators of plane Couette and Poiseuille flow are far from normal. With every eigenmode decaying, perturbations can grow transiently by O(R) and resonate by O(R²), and an operator perturbation of norm O(R⁻²) makes the flow eigenvalue-unstable, all read off the pseudospectra. That transition to turbulence then follows from linear growth plus energy-neutral nonlinear mixing is a conjecture, from a 2 × 2 model. | Read |
| [NOTE-842](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-842.md) | Farrell & Ioannou — Generalized Stability Theory II | For du/dt = A(t)u there are no modes, but the propagator's singular vectors and the Lyapunov exponents and vectors carry generalized stability theory over. A time-dependent operator that is stable, or neutral, at every instant can be asymptotically unstable, and only if it is non-normal. Random variation of the operator destabilizes generically, with less variation needed the more non-normal and the less damped the mean operator. | Read |
| [NOTE-851](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-851.md) | Ashby — Design for a Brain | Adaptation is the stability of the organism–environment system in the region where the essential variables stay within limits. To find such stability in an unknown environment, a second feedback must change the parameters of the first whenever an essential variable leaves its limits: the ultrastable system, shown in the Homeostat. Its blind search takes time exponential in the number of variables unless partial adaptations are kept, and keeping them needs a system that is not fully joined, its parts separated by constancies. New learning destroys old to the degree that it uses the same parts. | Read |
| [NOTE-935](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-935.md) | Seth — Measuring autonomy and emergence via Granger causality | G-autonomy ga_{X\|E} is the log ratio of a variable's prediction-error variance without and with its own past, given external variables E. G-emergence ge_{M\|m} = ga_{M\|m}·(1/N)Σ gc_{mᵢ→M} makes a macro variable emergent to the extent that it is both autonomous from and Granger-caused by its micro variables. Validated in a predator–prey model and a boids model, where flocking shows high G-emergence and Granger causation from the flock's centre of mass to each boid. Seth says the measures are relative to the predictor and the variables included. | Read |
| [NOTE-936](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-936.md) | Williams and Beer — Nonnegative decomposition of multivariate information | Redundancy is I_min(S; A₁…A_k) = Σ_s p(s) min_i I(S = s; A_i), the expected minimum specific information. Restricted to antichains of sources and ordered by α ≼ β iff every source of β contains one of α, the collections form a lattice. The Möbius inverse of I_min on it gives partial-information atoms that are nonnegative (Theorem 5) and sum to I(S; R). Interaction information is synergy minus redundancy for three variables and a signed mixture for four, which explains its negativity and its +1 bit for both 3-parity and three copies. | Read |
| [NOTE-937](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-937.md) | Bertschinger, Rauh, Olbrich, Jost and Ay — Quantifying unique information | For a target X and sources Y, Z, the unique information of Y is UĨ(X : Y \ Z) = min over Q ∈ Δ_P of MI_Q(X : Y \| Z), where Δ_P is the set of joints with the same (X,Y) and (X,Z) marginals. If unique information should depend only on those marginals, this is an upper bound on any such measure, and the shared and synergistic information it implies are lower bounds. It is zero exactly when the other source is Blackwell-sufficient. The measures are non-negative, satisfy the bivariate PI axioms and the identity property, and are a convex programme, but are bivariate only. | Read |
| [NOTE-940](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-940.md) | Schreiber — Measuring information transfer | Defines transfer entropy T_{J→I} as the Kullback entropy between I's transition probabilities with and without J's past, at history lengths k for I and l for J (Eq. 4), which is the conditional mutual information I(i_{n+1}; j_n^{(l)} \| i_n^{(k)}). It is directional and ignores static correlation. A kernel estimator is proposed. Tent-map and Ulam-map lattices show it detecting the coupling direction where time-delayed mutual information fails; a heart–breath pair shows an asymmetry that the author says a common trigger could also explain. | Read |
| [NOTE-942](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-942.md) | Williams and Beer — Generalized measures of information transfer | With the I_min partial information decomposition, transfer entropy T_{Y→X} = I(X_{t+1}; Y_t \| X_t) is the unique information of Y_t about X_{t+1} (state-independent transfer, SITE) plus the synergy of X_t and Y_t (state-dependent transfer, SDTE). SITE alone suffices for perfect open-loop controllability (Theorem 1). Time-delayed mutual information is SITE plus redundancy. Two-source transfer splits into unique, redundant and synergistic parts. On a sleep-apnoea recording, heart→breath transfer is all SDTE. | Read |
| [NOTE-943](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-943.md) | Lizier, Prokopenko and Zomaya — Local information transfer as a spatiotemporal filter | Transfer entropy is the expectation of a local transfer entropy, t_{Y→X}(n+1, k, l) = log p(x_{n+1} \| x⁽ᵏ⁾_n, y⁽ˡ⁾_n)/p(x_{n+1} \| x⁽ᵏ⁾_n), defined at every point and possibly negative. Apparent transfer entropy conditions on the destination's past; complete transfer entropy also on its other causal parents. On elementary cellular automata, with k ≥ 6 (rule 110) and k = 16, local transfer entropy highlights gliders and domain walls as the dominant information-transfer structures; k = 1 and local time-lagged mutual information do not. The averages carry none of this. | Read |
| [NOTE-944](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-944.md) v2 | Harder, Salge and Polani — A bivariate measure of redundant information | I_min gives 1 bit of redundancy to two independent bits copied into the target, because it compares amounts of specific information and not their direction in the space of distributions over the target. The paper adds an identity axiom, I∩((X,Y); X, Y) = I(X; Y), and defines a bivariate I_red: project each posterior p(z\|x) onto the convex hull of the other source's posteriors, count what survives, take the smaller direction. I_red satisfies all four axioms and gives a nonnegative PID. It agrees with I_min except where I_min overstates redundancy. | Read |
| [NOTE-945](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-945.md) | James, Barnett and Crutchfield — Information flows? A critique of transfer entropies | Information flow from X to Y is information in Y attributable solely to X's past. Transfer entropy is not it. For Y_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1} it is 1 bit, but the bit is synergistic, carried by both pasts jointly (co-information −1). For Z_t = X_{t−1} ⊕ Y_{t−1} both transfer entropies are 0, and the causation entropies (conditional transfer entropies) are 1 bit each, again localizing a joint bit. By PID, transfer entropy is unique plus synergistic information; conditioning adds synergy, it does not only remove redundancy. | Read |
| [NOTE-966](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-966.md) | Griffith and Koch — Quantifying synergistic mutual information | Synergy is the whole minus the union of its parts. S_VK = I(X_1…n : Y) − I_VK, where the union information I_VK is the least I*(X_1…n : Y) over joints that keep every source–target marginal. It sits between WholeMinusSum and S_max, which respectively subtract redundancy and count unique bits as synergy, and correlational importance measures something else. Versions 1–2 held that independent predictors share no information about the target; v6 withdraws it. For two predictors I_VK is Bertschinger et al.'s optimisation, so S_VK is their CI. | Read |
| [NOTE-967](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-967.md) | Griffith, Chong, James, Ellison and Crutchfield — Intersection information based on common randomness | The redundancy is the information about the target in the Gács–Körner common random variable of the sources, I_∧ = I(X_1 ∧ … ∧ X_n : Y): the largest I(Q : Y) for Q a function of every source. It is defined for any n, satisfies target monotonicity, which no earlier measure did, and lies below I_min. But it is zero whenever the sources have full support, so it fails identity and continuity, and its synergy goes negative. A zero-error variant satisfies identity in zero-error form and goes negative too. | Read |
| [NOTE-968](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-968.md) | Ince — Measuring multivariate redundant information with pointwise common change in surprisal | I_ccs measures redundancy as the expected local co-information over only those events where each source, the joint source and the overlap change the target's surprisal in the same direction, under the maximum-entropy joint matching source–target and joint-source marginals. Defined for any number of sources. It keeps symmetry, self-redundancy, subset equality and an independent-sources identity, and drops Harder et al.'s identity, monotonicity and non-negative atoms. A game-theoretic argument that unique information depends on the source–source marginal is offered against Bertschinger et al. | Read |
